vt.analysis:
Type: OpenClaw Skill
Name: naver-blog-writer
Version: 0.6.1

The skill relies on executing an external, scoped npm package (@y80163442/naver-thin-runner) via npx to install a local daemon and system services (--auto-service both) on macOS. It handles sensitive administrative API keys and tokens, and while these actions are consistent with the stated goal of automating Naver Blog publishing, the requirement for broad local system access and the execution of unverified remote code via npx represent a significant security risk.

llm.summary: The skill is a coherent Naver Blog publishing tool, but it asks users to run an unpinned third-party npm runner that can handle login, live publishing, and persistent local services.

dimensions.detail: The local runner is purpose-aligned, but it operates around browser-backed authentication, local tokens, setup/proof tokens, and possible control-plane credentials, with limited documentation of scope and containment.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: Setup, login, and daemon commands invoke npx @y80163442/naver-thin-runner without an exact version, lockfile, checksum, or provenance verification, so reviewed behavior is not tied to an immutable artifact.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The flow proceeds from readiness checks to setup, dry run, login, and publish_live, but it does not clearly require explicit user approval immediately before state-changing live publication or define target account/post visibility safeguards.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: The setup commands include --auto-service both and the skill can start a local daemon, but it does not document installed services, privileges, lifecycle, network exposure, or uninstall steps.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

dimensions.detail: The stated purpose is clear: publish prepared content to Naver Blog through an authenticated local browser. Live publishing and dry-run behavior are disclosed, but live external content changes would benefit from a stronger explicit confirmation requirement.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

llm.guidance: Review this carefully before installing. Treat publish_live as a real post to your Naver Blog account, avoid running the unpinned npx commands unless you trust the package source and current release, and ask for pinned versions, integrity verification, explicit live-publish confirmation, and documented service uninstall steps.
llm.findings:
[SQP-2] expected: Live publication is expected for this skill, and the artifact distinguishes dry_run from publish_live, but the concern is partly accepted because high-impact public posting lacks a prominent confirmation gate.
[RP1] unexpected: Using a local runner is expected, but repeatedly executing an unpinned npm package for setup, login, and daemon operations is not necessary to the purpose and creates material supply-chain risk.
[T06] expected: A daemon or service may fit a reliable local publishing endpoint, but automatic service installation is under-documented and lacks clear user control or removal instructions.
[T08] unexpected: The unpinned third-party npx execution is confirmed in the artifact and is a material concern because the effective code can change after review.
